title: Research
notice: Research preview. The pre-registered replay found no edge over the closing line; picks are market-anchored (10% model, 90% market) and graded publicly. Full launch 2027.
timeBound: Findings are time-bound: they describe 2024–2025 closing lines and say nothing about other seasons.

sections.heading: Is the closing line beatable by simple rules?
sections.summary: The consensus closing line behaved like a calibrated market. Simple side and total rules did not beat a coin flip, and nothing survived multiple-testing correction.

holm.label: Holm-adjusted p-values (report order)
holm.note: No test cleared a corrected threshold.

sections.heading: Walk-forward replay of the blend
sections.summary: The published blend leans 10% on the model and 90% on the closing market. It is statistically tied with the close. The models on their own were worse than the market.

blend.note: Fitted blend weight w≈0.09 against a fixed published weight of 0.10.

stats.label: R1 log loss, blend vs close
R3 model-side cover rate
stats.note: Not significant at this sample size.

sections.modelsAlone: Models alone were worse than the closing line.

sections.heading: Totals model (M4) holdout
sections.summary: The M4 total lean did not beat the closing total. When the model disagreed with the market by 3 or more points the lean still lost about half the time, and the market total was more accurate than M4 by 0.45 points of mean absolute error. Board total leans are labelled “no demonstrated edge”.

stats.label: Market total more accurate than M4 (MAE)

sections.heading: What these samples could and could not detect
sections.summary: A few hundred graded games can only expose very large edges. Detecting a one- or two-point ATS edge needs thousands of games, so the live record on this site is a public log, not evidence of skill.

footer: Derived values only. Lines shown are consensus medians, not individual sportsbook prices.
